alignments.note: Vocative noun; anarthrous, so no article competes.
Article of εὐδοκία. The ASV writes *my heart's desire*, whose determiner slot is already occupied by the genitive phrase rendered with *'s*; rule 20 empties the article.
Correlative μέν; the ASV writes no word for it (rule 70). A reference comparison will report this as a disagreement; that report is not a correction.
εὐδοκία rendered by the single word *desire*.
Article of καρδίας; the first-person possessive adjective ἐμῆς carries *my*, so the article realizes nothing (rule 54).
ἐμός names the possessor itself and takes *my* (rule 54).
Genitive noun rendered with the English prenominal possessive *heart's*.
No genitive pronoun stands here, so the supplied possessive *my* is the article's own under rule 20's second arm, not an `added` word (rule 11).
Article before θεόν; the ASV writes *God* with no determiner, so nothing anchors it (rules 21, 23).

Verbless clause: the prepositional predicate carries the supplied copula under rule 53, and rule 62 heads such a unit on the word realizing the preposition. Giving *is* instead to εἰς, the other prepositional phrase in the clause, remains defensible; I took ὑπέρ because the ASV writes *is for* together and εἰς already carries the whole supplied clause-introducer.
The preposition is realized by the word introducing its English clause (rules 40, 61), the ASV recasting εἰς σωτηρίαν as a finite purpose clause.
The verbal noun is rendered by the finite *they may be saved*; subject and auxiliaries are rule 7 helpers and rule 17 heads on the lexical verb.

review_notes: The supplied *my* at t006 is the article's under rule 20's second arm, since no genitive pronoun stands with δέησις; the ASV's italics are evidence, not a verdict (rule 11).
μέν is left unrepresented per rule 70's English-side test.
